senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; קָרָא)call, convocation. Sifra Emor, Par. 11, ch. XIV אלא אם עשאו מ׳ קדש unless one made it (the Day of Atonement) a holy call (observed it). Ib. ch. XIII, Par. 11 בני ישראל מ׳ קדש וכ׳ the sons of Israel are a holy convocation (called to celebrate the festivals) &c. Mekh. Bo. s. 9; a. fr.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:1">Ber. II, 1</cite> <he>זמן במ׳</he> the time for reading the sh’mʿa.
<cite ref="Megillah 3a:17">Meg. 3ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מ׳ מגילה</he> the recitation of the Book of Esther.

<cite ref="Tosefta Berakhot 2:20">Tosef. Ber. II, 20</cite> <he>יש שם מ׳ ותפלה</he> reading the Scriptures and prayer are permitted there; <cite ref="Shabbat 10a:11">Sabb. 10ᵃ</cite>; a. e.—Meg. l. c. (ref. to <cite ref="Nehemiah 8:8">Neh. VIII, 8</cite> <he>ויקראו מ׳</he>) <he>זו</he> this means the reading of the text; <cite ref="Nedarim 37b:6">Ned. 37ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: pronunciation, vocalization; מ׳ סופרים the traditional vocalization of the Scripture texts. Ib.

teaching the Bible, primary instruction. Ib. IV, 3 לא ילמדנו מ׳ he must not teach him Bible, contrad. to מדרש &c. Ib. 36ᵇ bot. במקום … על המ׳ where is it customary to take remuneration for teaching the Bible.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:1:4">Y. Meg. III, beg. 73ᵈ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 13:1:2">Y. Keth. XIII, beg. 35ᶜ</cite> <he>בית ספר למ׳ וכ׳</he> Beth Sepher was the school for Bible, Beth Talmud for Mishnah.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 2">Lev. R. s. 2</cite>, beg. <he>נכנסין למ׳</he> enter the primary school; a. fr.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:2:15">Y. Taan. IV, 68ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>חיזרנו על כל המ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H00560"><he>חָזַר</he></cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 5:2">Sot. V, 2</cite> <he>שאין לו מ׳ מן התורה וכ׳</he> there is for it no passage in the Torah intimating that it is unclean.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 5:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מביא לו מ׳ מן וכ׳</he> produces for it a Biblical text in evidence &c.

<cite ref="Yevamot 11b:9">Yeb. 11ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>אין מ׳ יוצא מידי פשוטו</he> a Bible verse can never lose its literal sense (although its meaning may be extended by the methods of interpretation).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 34a:11">Snh. 34ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מ׳ אחד יוצא וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="I00611"><he>טַעַם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 101a:10">Ib. 101ᵃ</cite> <he>מ׳ זה מעצמו נדרש</he> this verse must be interpreted from its own wording.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 101a:10">Ib.</cite> bot. <he>מנין לך … מ׳ אני דורש</he> how do you know this?… I interpret Bible verses; a. fr.—Pl. <he>מִקְרָאוֹת</he>, <he>מִקְרָיוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Menachot 19b:11">Men. 19ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Zevachim 63b:6">Zeb. 63ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sotah 14b:14">Sot. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>כ״מ שאתה מוצא שני מ׳ אחד וכ׳</he> wherever there are two possible interpretations of two parallel expressions one of which contradicts the other, and one of which confirms the other &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 8:8:2">Y. Snh. VIII, 26ᶜ</cite> top <he>זה אחד משלשה מ׳</he> this is one of the three passages where the Law speaks metaphorically; Y. Keth. IV, 28ᶜ top; a. fr.
